stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on May 11th.
stocks.news: A quiet Monday tape with all three indices grinding slightly green. The interesting moves were under the surface. Bio stocks spiked then faded on news of a hantavirus outbreak tied to a Dutch cruise ship (8 cases, 3 deaths). The WHO is calling public health risk low, but trial-pipeline names ran briefly: Moderna (MRNA -2.70%), Novavax (NVAX -6.03%), Inovio (INO -2.05%) all closed red after intraday pops. Sony Music (SONY +5.66%) went on a $4B catalog buying spree, picking up 45,000+ songs from Blackstone (BX -1.88%) including Beyonce, Fleetwood Mac, and Rihanna tracks. Warner (WMG -1.26%), Spotify (SPOT +0.40%), and Amazon (AMZN -1.35%) are chasing the same shelf, treating music catalogs as recurring-revenue infrastructure. Trump heads to China this week with Musk and Tim Cook in tow, alongside the CEOs of Boeing (BA +0.34%), BlackRock (BLK -0.30%), and Goldman Sachs (GS +0.87%). Trade, rare earths, and Taiwan are on the agenda.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 11th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year stepped up to 4.41% (+0.04%), gold ticked higher to $4,745, and WTI ripped another 3.96% to $101.95, the second straight session of major energy moves. Brent at $104.63 (+3.30%). The Iran war premium is now built into the curve.

The big macro shift is across the Atlantic. European economists now expect the ECB to HIKE rates twice this year, reversing the prior one-cut outlook. Iran-driven oil prices pushed euro-area inflation forecasts to 2.7% for 2026. For U.S. investors, higher rates in Europe means higher rates for longer at home, which is exactly the tape mortgages are now reading.

Gas at $4.50 is splitting the restaurant industry in two. Fast food (Burger King, McDonald's MCD -0.42%) saw sales rise last quarter; casual dining is collapsing. Applebee's parent Dine Brands (DIN +2.43%) says diners pull back once gas tops $3.50, and 43% of drivers have already cut back on dining out. Trump is reportedly considering temporarily suspending the federal gas tax, a discretionary-budget release valve if it lands.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on May 11th.
crypto.commentary: Bitcoin held the $81,000 line at $81,190 (-1.21%), ETH at $2,345, XRP at $1.45. The story is in flows and regulation, not price. Crypto fund inflows hit $857M last week, more than seven times the prior week, with Bitcoin scooping $706M of that. The catalyst was a Senate compromise on the CLARITY Act and stablecoin rules, the first real clarity on U.S. crypto regulation in years. Separately, Circle (CRCL +15.91%) just raised $222M in the first ICO by a U.S. public company, a new template that other public companies will watch closely.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates Pop 10 BPs On Iran And ECB Hawks; April Existing Sales Stall At +0.2%; Blackstone Funds 50K Builder Homes
real_estate.commentary:
Three real-estate stories worth weaving together for client conversations this week.

First, mortgage rates jumped sharply overnight. The 30-year sits at 6.52% (+10 bps) today, the 15-year at 6.03% (+4 bps). Yesterday's rates were 6.42% and 5.99%. A 10-basis-point jump is the largest one-day move we've seen since the early-2026 inflation prints. The driver is global: Iran-driven oil at $102 plus ECB now signaling rate HIKES equals a sudden repricing of duration risk worldwide. For a $1.2M Fremont purchase at 20% down, the monthly payment difference between 6.42% and 6.52% is roughly $63 a month. Not huge in absolute terms, but it's a real qualification shift for buyers near the DTI line.

Second, April existing home sales barely moved (+0.2%) versus consensus of +3%. The median sale price hit a fresh April record at $417,700. The catch: first-time buyers held just 33% of sales. The price ceiling plus the new rate jump is going to tighten the first-time buyer pool further. Sellers pricing for "the buyer who's been qualified for months" need to be ready to negotiate.

Third, Blackstone is launching a new lender to fund 50,000 new homes a year. The firm's real-estate debt arm will lend directly to builders. The U.S. is now building fewer homes annually than in 1960, despite a population that has nearly doubled. The new-construction segment was already pricing aggressively (last week we covered builder discounts taking new-home prices to a five-year low). Blackstone funding the pipeline is a structural shift, not a cyclical one.

Total active inventory across the 15-city board is 2,862, down 29 from Monday. 224 new listings today, slight cool from Monday's 237. 226 closed sales for the week, four more than Monday's print. Tuesday came in steady, no major rotation.

For listing agents: the 10-bp rate jump is real and your active buyers are doing the math right now. The qualified ones who were in contract or close to it will likely absorb it. The fence-sitters may pause. Suggested play: reach out to any prospect who said "let me know if rates drop", they need to hear that the trend is reversing, not falling. Time-on-market for fence-sitters got shorter today.

For buyer agents: with Blackstone funding builder pipelines and Iran and ECB pushing rates the wrong way, the buyer who pulls the trigger this month is buying ahead of a structural floor on inventory and ahead of further rate creep. Make that case explicit in your next conversation.
